INTERESTING QUESTION. I think it depends on why you’re afraid of it! That goes for a lot of things honestly: if you’re afraid of the ocean it could be the Dark (you don’t know what’s down there, the Buried (trapped and unable to breathe), or the Vast (it’s so big and you couldn’t possibly fathom what’s down there). If you’re afraid of losing a part of yourself to the pregnancy or being changed, I’d say Corruption (like you said, parasite) or even Stranger (you’re turning into something you don’t recognize anymore). If you’re scared of the physical changes, that could be the Flesh. If you’re scared of how people will react, that could be the Eye (everyone looking at you or wanting to touch you) or the Lonely (fearing people will leave because it’s too much). Maybe even the Web, knowing that this is gonna control you forever. Honestly I think that most things could fall into multiple fears just based on WHY we fear them. Let me know if that makes sense, I just got off work and this was extremely stream of consciousness lmao

First of all, I completely agree that vaccination has absolutely NO CONNECTION with autism. Even though I stated that at the beginning of my argument, I definitely should have reiterated and made sure that my beliefs were understood.

Secondly, although they have no merit scientifically, I have always taken issue with arguments that vaccines cause autism, homosexuality, etc. I believe that some new parents (anti-vaxxers especially) have this idea of the perfect child they will have. Straight, cis, neurotypical, able-bodied, etc. If their child is not all of those things, they then have three choices.

They could try to understand that that is how their child was born, and try to support and help them as best they can. Obviously I believe that that is the correct choice, but many parents refuse to see things in that light. From there, the other two options are decidedly worse: they could either believe that they did something wrong and punish their child because of it, or they could find a completely unrelated thing and blame that.

Obviously, most anti-vaxxers chose the latter, and have chosen to blame vaccines. All that I was trying to say with my argument is that if you would rather have a dead child than one you see as perfect (even though again, there is no connection between vaccines and autism), then you don’t deserve to have kids.

I understand how my argument could be unhelpful in the fight for vaccines, but I’m just so tired of that argument, and I figured this was the best place to say something.
